subject: Mathematics
title: Mean Deviation About Mean and Median
formulaOrRule: MD(\bar{x}) = \frac{1}{N} \sum_{i=1}^N |x_i - \bar{x}|, \quad MD(M) = \frac{1}{N} \sum_{i=1}^N |x_i - M|
derivationOrExplanation: By definition, mean deviation is the average absolute difference of all observations from a measure of central tendency. Differentiating $\sum |x_i - c|$ with respect to $c$ changes sign at each point; the derivative is zero when the number of points below $c$ equals points above $c$, which occurs exactly at the median $M$. Hence, Mean Deviation is minimal when measured about the Median.

title: Poisson Distribution for Rare Events
formulaOrRule: P(X = k) = \frac{\lambda^k e^{-\lambda}}{k!} \quad (k = 0, 1, 2, \dots), \quad E[X] = \text{Var}(X) = \lambda

variablesOrTerms.\\lambda = n p: average rate of occurrences per interval

derivationOrExplanation: Take Poisson limit of binomial distribution as $n \to \infty, p \to 0$ with $np = \lambda$: $P(X = k) = \binom{n}{k} p^k (1 - p)^{n - k} = \frac{n(n-1)\dots(n-k+1)}{k!} \left(\frac{\lambda}{n}\right)^k \left(1 - \frac{\lambda}{n}\right)^n \left(1 - \frac{\lambda}{n}\right)^{-k}$. As $n \to \infty$: $\frac{n(n-1)\dots(n-k+1)}{n^k} \to 1$, $(1 - \lambda/n)^n \to e^{-\lambda}$, and $(1 - \lambda/n)^{-k} \to 1$. Hence $P(X = k) = \frac{\lambda^k e^{-\lambda}}{k!}$.

subject: Mathematics
title: Karl Pearson's Empirical Relation for Moderately Skewed Distributions
formulaOrRule: \text{Mode} \approx 3 \text{ Median} - 2 \text{ Mean}
derivationOrExplanation: In a symmetric distribution: Mean = Median = Mode. In a moderately skewed unimodal frequency distribution, the median approximately divides the distance from mean to mode in a 2:1 ratio: $\text{Mean} - \text{Median} \approx \frac{1}{3}(\text{Mean} - \text{Mode}) \implies 3(\text{Mean} - \text{Median}) \approx \text{Mean} - \text{Mode} \implies \text{Mode} \approx 3\text{Median} - 2\text{Mean}$.

title: Multiplication Rule of Probability
formulaOrRule: P(A | B) = \frac{P(A \cap B)}{P(B)} \implies P(A \cap B) = P(B) P(A | B) = P(A) P(B | A)
derivationOrExplanation: Follows from definition of conditional probability: the probability that event $A$ occurs given that event $B$ has already occurred is the proportion of outcomes in $B$ that also belong to $A$: $P(A | B) = \frac{n(A \cap B)}{n(B)} = \frac{n(A \cap B)/n(S)}{n(B)/n(S)} = \frac{P(A \cap B)}{P(B)}$. Multiplying both sides by $P(B)$ gives $P(A \cap B) = P(B) P(A | B)$.

title: Magnetic Field of Straight Current-Carrying Conductor
formulaOrRule: B = \frac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi d} \quad (\text{Infinite Wire}), \quad B = \frac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi d}(\sin\alpha + \sin\beta) \quad (\text{Finite Wire})

variablesOrTerms.\\alpha, \\beta: Angles subtended by wire endpoints at the point

derivationOrExplanation: From Biot-Savart law: $dl = d\sec^2\theta d\theta$, $r = d\sec\theta$. Then $dB = \frac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi} \frac{\cos\theta dl}{r^2} = \frac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi d}\cos\theta d\theta$. Integrating from $-\beta$ to $\alpha$: $B = \frac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi d}[\sin\alpha - \sin(-\beta)] = \frac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi d}(\sin\alpha + \sin\beta)$. For infinite wire, $\alpha = \beta = 90^\circ \implies B = \frac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi d}$.

title: Magnetic Field on Axis and Center of Circular Current Loop
formulaOrRule: B_{axial} = \frac{\mu_0 N I R^2}{2(R^2 + x^2)^{3/2}}, \quad B_{center} = \frac{\mu_0 N I}{2R}
derivationOrExplanation: Element $I d\vec{l}$ is perpendicular to $\vec{r}$ where $r = \sqrt{R^2 + x^2}$. Differential field is $dB = \frac{\mu_0 I dl}{4\pi r^2}$. Components perpendicular to the axis cancel by symmetry around the ring. The axial component is $dB_x = dB\sin\theta = dB\left(\frac{R}{r}\right) = \frac{\mu_0 I R dl}{4\pi (R^2 + x^2)^{3/2}}$. Integrating over loop circumference $\oint dl = 2\pi R$ and multiplying by $N$ turns gives $B = \frac{\mu_0 N I R^2}{2(R^2 + x^2)^{3/2}}$. Setting $x=0$ yields center field $B = \frac{\mu_0 N I}{2R}$.

title: Force Between Parallel Current-Carrying Conductors
formulaOrRule: \frac{F}{L} = \frac{\mu_0}{2\pi}\frac{I_1 I_2}{d}

title: Torque and Potential Energy of Magnetic Dipole
formulaOrRule: \vec{\tau} = \vec{M} \times \vec{B}, \quad U = -\vec{M} \cdot \vec{B}, \quad \vec{M} = N I A \hat{n}
derivationOrExplanation: For rectangular loop of sides $a$ and $b$ in field $B$: forces on sides of length $a$ are $F = I a B$ forming a couple of lever arm $b\sin\theta$. title: Magnetic Susceptibility and Temperature Dependence
formulaOrRule: \chi_m = \frac{C}{T} \quad (\text{Curie's Law}), \quad \chi_m = \frac{C}{T - T_c} \quad (\text{Curie-Weiss Law})
derivationOrExplanation: Paramagnetism arises from alignment of permanent atomic dipoles against randomizing thermal agitation ($k_B T$). title: Bohr Magneton
formulaOrRule: \mu_B = \frac{e \hbar}{2 m_e} \approx 9.274 \times 10^{-24} \text{ A m}^2 = \text{J/T}
derivationOrExplanation: Orbital current of electron in circular orbit of radius $r$ and period $T = 2\pi r/v$ is $I = e/T = \frac{ev}{2\pi r}$. title: Hall Effect Voltage and Hall Coefficient
formulaOrRule: V_H = \frac{I B}{n q d} = \frac{R_H I B}{d}, \quad R_H = \frac{1}{n q}

title: Fundamental Permutations and Combinations Formulas
formulaOrRule: ^n P_r = \frac{n!}{(n - r)!}, \quad ^n C_r = \binom{n}{r} = \frac{n!}{r!(n - r)!}
derivationOrExplanation: To arrange $r$ distinct items out of $n$: First position has $n$ choices, second has $n-1$, ..., $r$-th has $n-(r-1) = n-r+1$ choices. Total arrangements $= n(n-1)\dots(n-r+1) = \frac{n!}{(n-r)!} = ^n P_r$. Since each selection of $r$ items can be ordered in $r!$ ways, the number of unordered combinations is $\binom{n}{r} = \frac{^n P_r}{r!} = \frac{n!}{r!(n-r)!}$.

title: Pascal's Combinatorial Identity
formulaOrRule: \binom{n}{r} + \binom{n}{r - 1} = \binom{n + 1}{r}
derivationOrExplanation: Algebraic proof: $\frac{n!}{r!(n-r)!} + \frac{n!}{(r-1)!(n-r+1)!} = \frac{n!}{(r-1)!(n-r)!}\left[\frac{1}{r} + \frac{1}{n-r+1}\right] = \frac{n!}{(r-1)!(n-r)!}\left[\frac{n+1}{r(n-r+1)}\right] = \frac{(n+1)!}{r!(n+1-r)!} = \binom{n+1}{r}$. Combinatorial proof: To pick $r$ elements from $n+1$ elements (including fixed element $X$), either include $X$ (choose remaining $r-1$ from $n$) or exclude $X$ (choose $r$ from $n$).

title: Circular Permutations of n Distinct Objects
formulaOrRule: P_{circle} = (n - 1)!, \quad P_{necklace} = \frac{(n - 1)!}{2}
derivationOrExplanation: Linear arrangements equal $n!$. In a circle, rotating an arrangement preserves relative circular order, so each distinct circular arrangement generates $n$ equivalent linear arrangements by shifting starting points. Hence distinct circular permutations $= n! / n = (n - 1)!$. If clockwise and counter-clockwise directions are indistinguishable (e.g. bead necklace flipped over), divide by 2: $(n - 1)! / 2$.

title: Permutations of Multiset with Repeated Elements
formulaOrRule: N = \frac{n!}{p! \, q! \, r!} \quad (p + q + r = n)
derivationOrExplanation: If all $n$ items were distinct, total arrangements would be $n!$. However, swapping the $p$ identical items among themselves in any of their $p!$ internal positions leaves the overall sequence unchanged. Likewise for $q!$ and $r!$. By the multiplication principle of counting, total distinguishable permutations $= \frac{n!}{p! q! r!}$.

title: Derangements Formula (No object in its original place)
formulaOrRule: D_n = n! \sum_{k=0}^n \frac{(-1)^k}{k!} = n!\left(1 - \frac{1}{1!} + \frac{1}{2!} - \frac{1}{3!} + \dots + \frac{(-1)^n}{n!}\right)

title: Total Non-empty Selections from Multiset

variablesOrTerms.p, q, r: counts of identical items of type A, B, C

derivationOrExplanation: For items of type A (which are identical), we can select 0, 1, 2, ..., up to $p$ items, giving $p + 1$ choices. title: Sum of Divisors of Positive Integer N
formulaOrRule: \sigma(N) = \prod_{i=1}^k \frac{p_i^{a_i + 1} - 1}{p_i - 1}
derivationOrExplanation: Expand the algebraic product $(1 + p_1 + p_1^2 + \dots + p_1^{a_1})(1 + p_2 + \dots + p_2^{a_2})\dots(1 + p_k + \dots + p_k^{a_k})$. Multiplying out produces every single divisor of $N$ exactly once. Each factor is a finite geometric series: $1 + p + \dots + p^a = \frac{p^{a+1} - 1}{p - 1}$. Multiplying these geometric sums gives $\prod \frac{p_i^{a_i+1}-1}{p_i-1}$.

title: Angle of Friction and Angle of Repose
formulaOrRule: \theta_s = \tan^{-1}(\mu_s), \quad \theta_r = \tan^{-1}(\mu_s)

title: Maximum Safe Speed on a Banked Road
formulaOrRule: v_{max} = \sqrt{\frac{R g (\mu_s + \tan\theta)}{1 - \mu_s \tan\theta}}
derivationOrExplanation: At impending outward slip, friction $f = \mu_s N$ acts downwards along the incline. Resolving vertically: $N\cos\theta - f\sin\theta = mg \implies N(\cos\theta - \mu_s\sin\theta) = mg$. Resolving horizontally for centripetal force: $N\sin\theta + f\cos\theta = \frac{m v^2}{R} \implies N(\sin\theta + \mu_s\cos\theta) = \frac{m v^2}{R}$. Dividing horizontal by vertical equation: $\frac{v_{max}^2}{Rg} = \frac{\sin\theta + \mu_s\cos\theta}{\cos\theta - \mu_s\sin\theta} = \frac{\tan\theta + \mu_s}{1 - \mu_s\tan\theta}$.

title: Pseudo Force (D'Alembert Force)
formulaOrRule: \vec{F}_{pseudo} = -m\vec{a}_0

variablesOrTerms.\\vec{a}_0: Acceleration of reference frame w.r.t. ground

derivationOrExplanation: In inertial frame, $\vec{F}_{real} = m\vec{a}_{in}$. If frame has acceleration $\vec{a}_0$, acceleration of particle relative to frame is $\vec{a}_{rel} = \vec{a}_{in} - \vec{a}_0$. Multiplying by mass $m$: $m\vec{a}_{rel} = m\vec{a}_{in} - m\vec{a}_0 = \vec{F}_{real} + (-m\vec{a}_0)$. Defining $\vec{F}_{pseudo} = -m\vec{a}_0$ restores $\sum \vec{F} = m\vec{a}_{rel}$.

title: Tsiolkovsky Rocket Equation with Gravity
formulaOrRule: v(t) = v_0 + v_{rel} \ln\left(\frac{m_0}{m(t)}\right) - gt
derivationOrExplanation: Momentum balance for system at time $t$ and $t+dt$: $(m-dm)(v+dv) + dm(v - v_{rel}) - mv = -mg\,dt$. Neglecting second-order differential $dm\,dv$: $m\,dv - v_{rel}dm = -mg\,dt \implies dv = -v_{rel}\frac{dm}{m} - g\,dt$. Integrating from $m_0$ to $m(t)$: $v(t) - v_0 = v_{rel}\ln(m_0/m) - gt$.

title: String Tension at Arbitrary Angle in Simple Pendulum
formulaOrRule: T(\theta) = m g (3\cos\theta - 2\cos\theta_0)
derivationOrExplanation: By energy conservation: $mgL(\cos\theta - \cos\theta_0) = \frac{1}{2}m v^2 \implies \frac{mv^2}{L} = 2mg(\cos\theta - \cos\theta_0)$. Radially, Newton's law gives $T - mg\cos\theta = \frac{mv^2}{L}$. Substituting $\frac{mv^2}{L}$: $T = mg\cos\theta + 2mg(\cos\theta - \cos\theta_0) = mg(3\cos\theta - 2\cos\theta_0)$.

title: Acceleration of Movable Wedge on Smooth Floor
formulaOrRule: a_{wedge} = \frac{m g \sin\alpha \cos\alpha}{M + m\sin^2\alpha}

title: Relation Between Partial Pressure and Molar Concentration Equilibrium Constants
formulaOrRule: K_p = K_c (R T)^{\Delta n_g}, \quad \Delta n_g = \sum \nu_{g, prod} - \sum \nu_{g, react}

title: Reaction Quotient (Q) Spontaneity Direction Criterion
formulaOrRule: Q < K \implies \text{Forward Shift}, \quad Q = K \implies \text{Equilibrium}, \quad Q > K \implies \text{Reverse Shift}
derivationOrExplanation: From $\Delta_r G = \Delta_r G^\circ + RT\ln Q$ and $\Delta_r G^\circ = -RT\ln K$: $\Delta_r G = -RT\ln K + RT\ln Q = RT\ln(Q/K)$. If $Q < K$, then $\ln(Q/K) < 0 \implies \Delta_r G < 0$, so reaction proceeds spontaneously in the forward direction. If $Q > K$, $\Delta_r G > 0$, so reaction proceeds in the reverse direction. If $Q = K$, $\Delta_r G = 0$, system is in dynamic equilibrium.

title: Ostwald's Dilution Law for Weak Monoprotic Acids
formulaOrRule: \alpha = \sqrt{\frac{K_a}{C}}, \quad [H^+] = \sqrt{K_a C}, \quad pH = \frac{1}{2}(pK_a - \log C) \quad (\alpha \le 0.05)
derivationOrExplanation: Equilibrium: $HA \rightleftharpoons H^+ + A^-$. Equilibrium concentrations: $[HA] = C(1-\alpha)$, $[H^+] = C\alpha$, $[A^-] = C\alpha$. Acid constant is $K_a = \frac{[H^+][A^-]}{[HA]} = \frac{(C\alpha)(C\alpha)}{C(1-\alpha)} = \frac{C\alpha^2}{1-\alpha}$. For weak electrolytes where $\alpha \ll 1$ (typically $\alpha \le 0.05$), approximation $1 - \alpha \approx 1$ gives $K_a \approx C\alpha^2 \implies \alpha = \sqrt{K_a / C}$. Hydronium is $[H^+] = C\alpha = C\sqrt{K_a/C} = \sqrt{K_a C}$. Taking negative logarithm: $pH = -\log\sqrt{K_a C} = \frac{1}{2}(pK_a - \log C)$.

title: Henderson-Hasselbalch Equation for Acidic Buffers
formulaOrRule: pH = pK_a + \log_{10}\left(\frac{[\text{Conjugate Base}]}{[\text{Weak Acid}]}\right) = pK_a + \log\left(\frac{[\text{Salt}]}{[\text{Acid}]}\right)

title: Henderson-Hasselbalch Equation for Basic Buffers
formulaOrRule: pOH = pK_b + \log_{10}\left(\frac{[\text{Conjugate Acid}]}{[\text{Weak Base}]}\right), \quad pH + pOH = pK_w = 14 \quad (25^\circ\text{C})

title: Hydrolysis of Salt of Weak Acid and Strong Base
formulaOrRule: pH = 7 + \frac{1}{2}pK_a + \frac{1}{2}\log C \quad (\text{Salt of Weak Acid & Strong Base, e.g. } CH_3COONa)
derivationOrExplanation: Anion hydrolysis: $A^- + H_2O \rightleftharpoons HA + OH^-$. Equilibrium: $K_h = \frac{[HA][OH^-]}{[A^-]} = \frac{K_w}{K_a}$. Then $[H^+] = \frac{K_w}{[OH^-]} = \sqrt{\frac{K_w K_a}{C}}$. Taking negative logarithm: $pH = -\frac{1}{2}\log K_w - \frac{1}{2}\log K_a + \frac{1}{2}\log C = 7 + \frac{1}{2}pK_a + \frac{1}{2}\log C$.

title: Solubility Product Constant ($K_{sp}$) and Molar Solubility (S)
formulaOrRule: K_{sp} = x^x y^y S^{x+y} \implies S = \left(\frac{K_{sp}}{x^x y^y}\right)^{\frac{1}{x+y}}
derivationOrExplanation: Dissolution equilibrium: $A_x B_{y(s)} \rightleftharpoons x A^{y+}_{(aq)} + y B^{x-}_{(aq)}$. If molar solubility is $S$, then ion concentrations at saturation are $[A^{y+}] = x S$ and $[B^{x-}] = y S$. The solubility product is $K_{sp} = [A^{y+}]^x [B^{x-}]^y = (x S)^x (y S)^y = x^x y^y S^{x+y}$. Solving for $S$ gives $S = \left(\frac{K_{sp}}{x^x y^y}\right)^{1/(x+y)}$.

title: Ionic Product ($Q_{sp}$) and Precipitation Condition
formulaOrRule: Q_{sp} > K_{sp} \implies \text{Precipitation}, \quad Q_{sp} = K_{sp} \implies \text{Saturated}, \quad Q_{sp} < K_{sp} \implies \text{Unsaturated}
derivationOrExplanation: Analogous to chemical reaction quotient: ionic product $Q_{sp} = [A^{y+}]_{initial}^x [B^{x-}]_{initial}^y$ evaluates current ion concentrations. If $Q_{sp} < K_{sp}$, solution can dissolve more solid (unsaturated). If $Q_{sp} = K_{sp}$, solution is at exact dynamic saturation. If $Q_{sp} > K_{sp}$, solution is supersaturated; excess ions spontaneously precipitate out of solution until remaining ion product equals $K_{sp}$.

title: Effect of pH on Solubility of Sparingly Soluble Salts
formulaOrRule: S' = S \sqrt{1 + \frac{[H^+]}{K_a}} \quad (\text{Solubility of Basic Anion in Acid})

variablesOrTerms.K_a: Dissociation constant of conjugate weak acid

derivationOrExplanation: For salt $MA \rightleftharpoons M^+ + A^-$, anion reacts with acid: $A^- + H^+ \rightleftharpoons HA$ with $K = 1/K_a$. Total dissolved salt is $S' = [M^+] = [A^-] + [HA] = [A^-]\left(1 + \frac{[H^+]}{K_a}\right)$. Then $K_{sp} = [M^+][A^-] = S' \frac{S'}{1 + [H^+]/K_a} = \frac{(S')^2}{1 + [H^+]/K_a}$. Solving gives $S' = \sqrt{K_{sp}\left(1 + \frac{[H^+]}{K_a}\right)} = S\sqrt{1 + \frac{[H^+]}{K_a}}$.

title: pH of Amphiprotic Species (Polyprotic Intermediate Ions)
formulaOrRule: [H^+] = \sqrt{K_{a1} K_{a2}} \implies pH = \frac{pK_{a1} + pK_{a2}}{2} \quad (\text{Amphiprotic Ion, e.g. } HCO_3^-, H_2PO_4^-)

title: Isoelectric Point (pI) of Amino Acids
formulaOrRule: pH_{isoelectric} = pI = \frac{pK_{a1} + pK_{a2}}{2}
derivationOrExplanation: At isoelectric point, concentration of cationic form ($H_2A^+$) strictly equals concentration of anionic form ($A^-$): $[H_2A^+] = [A^-]$. Taking negative log gives $pI = \frac{pK_{a1} + pK_{a2}}{2}$.

title: Drift Velocity and Current Density Relation
formulaOrRule: I = n A q v_d, \quad v_d = \frac{e E}{m}\tau
derivationOrExplanation: Between collisions, electrons accelerate under electric field: $a = \frac{eE}{m}$. Average drift speed acquired between collisions is $v_d = a\tau = \frac{eE}{m}\tau$. Volume of charge passing cross-section $A$ in time $\Delta t$ is $\Delta V = A v_d \Delta t$. Total charge is $\Delta Q = n(A v_d \Delta t)e$. Dividing by $\Delta t$: $I = \frac{\Delta Q}{\Delta t} = n e A v_d$.

title: Resistance, Resistivity and Temperature Coefficient
formulaOrRule: R = \rho \frac{L}{A} = \frac{m}{n e^2 \tau}\frac{L}{A}, \quad R(T) = R_0 [1 + \alpha(T - T_0)]
derivationOrExplanation: From microscopic Ohm's law $J = \sigma E$, we have $E = \rho J = \rho \frac{I}{A}$. Voltage across length $L$ is $V = E L = \left(\rho \frac{L}{A}\right)I = R I \implies R = \rho \frac{L}{A}$. For metals, increased lattice thermal vibrations decrease relaxation time $\tau$, causing resistivity to rise linearly near room temperature: $\rho(T) = \rho_0(1 + \alpha \Delta T)$.

title: Raoult's Law for Ideal Binary Liquid Mixtures
formulaOrRule: P_A = P_A^\circ x_A, \quad P_{total} = P_A^\circ x_A + P_B^\circ x_B = P_B^\circ + (P_A^\circ - P_B^\circ)x_A

variablesOrTerms.P_A, P_B: Partial vapor pressures of components A and B
variablesOrTerms.P_A^\\circ, P_B^\\circ: Vapor pressures of pure components A and B

derivationOrExplanation: Francois-Marie Raoult (1887) observed that escaping tendency of volatile solvent molecules from liquid surface into vapor phase is directly proportional to surface fraction of that component. In an ideal solution with identical intermolecular forces ($A-A \approx B-B \approx A-B$), surface mole fraction equals bulk liquid mole fraction $x_A$, giving $P_A = P_A^\circ x_A$. Dalton's law of partial pressures gives $P_{total} = P_A + P_B = P_A^\circ x_A + P_B^\circ(1 - x_A) = P_B^\circ + (P_A^\circ - P_B^\circ)x_A$.

title: Relative Lowering of Vapor Pressure (RLVP)
formulaOrRule: \frac{P_1^\circ - P_1}{P_1^\circ} = i \cdot x_2 \approx i \cdot \frac{n_2}{n_1} = i \cdot \frac{w_2 M_1}{M_2 w_1}

title: van 't Hoff Equation for Osmotic Pressure
formulaOrRule: \Pi = i \cdot C R T = i \cdot \frac{n_2}{V} R T = i \cdot \frac{w_2}{M_2 V} R T
derivationOrExplanation: Jacobus Henricus van 't Hoff (1887) recognized thermodynamic equivalence between dilute solute molecules in solvent and ideal gas molecules in vacuum: chemical potential of pure solvent across membrane at pressure $P + \Pi$ must equal solution chemical potential at pressure $P$: $\mu_1^\circ(P + \Pi) = \mu_1(P) = \mu_1^\circ(P) + RT\ln x_1$. Expanding $\mu_1^\circ(P + \Pi) - \mu_1^\circ(P) = \int_P^{P+\Pi} V_m dP = \Pi V_m$. Using $\ln x_1 = \ln(1 - x_2) \approx -x_2 = -n_2 / n_1$: $\Pi V_m = RT(n_2 / n_1) \implies \Pi (n_1 V_m) = n_2 RT$. Since $n_1 V_m = V$ (total solution volume): $\Pi V = n_2 RT \implies \Pi = CRT$. Multiplying by $i$ for electrolytes gives $\Pi = iCRT$.

title: van 't Hoff Factor (i) Relations for Dissociation and Association
formulaOrRule: i = 1 + (n - 1)\alpha \quad (\text{Dissociation}), \quad i = 1 - \left(1 - \frac{1}{n}\right)\beta \quad (\text{Association})

variablesOrTerms.n: Number of ions produced per formula unit

derivationOrExplanation: Dissociation: 1 mole of $A_n$ dissociates to give $(1-\alpha)$ moles of reactant and $n\alpha$ moles of ions. Total particles in solution is $N_{total} = (1-\alpha) + n\alpha = 1 + (n-1)\alpha$. By definition $i = \frac{\text{Actual moles}}{\text{Theoretical moles}} = \frac{1 + (n-1)\alpha}{1} = 1 + (n-1)\alpha$. Association: $n A \rightleftharpoons A_n$. Starting with 1 mole: remaining monomer is $1-\beta$, associated cluster is $\beta/n$. Total particles: $N_{total} = (1-\beta) + \beta/n = 1 - \left(1 - \frac{1}{n}\right)\beta \implies i = 1 - \left(1 - \frac{1}{n}\right)\beta$.

formulaOrRule: \frac{1}{y_A} = \frac{x_A}{P_A^\circ} P_{total} \implies P_{total} = \frac{P_A^\circ P_B^\circ}{P_A^\circ + (P_B^\circ - P_A^\circ)y_A}

title: Ionic Strength and Debye-Huckel Limiting Law for Mean Activity Coefficients
formulaOrRule: I = \frac{1}{2}\sum c_i z_i^2, \quad \log_{10} \gamma_\pm = -0.509 |z_+ z_-| \sqrt{I} \quad (\text{Debye-Huckel Limiting Law})
derivationOrExplanation: Gilbert Lewis introduced ionic strength $I = \frac{1}{2}\sum c_i z_i^2$ to quantify the electrostatic field intensity generated by all ions. Debye and Huckel (1923) solved the linearized Poisson-Boltzmann equation for the ion cloud screening potential: the electrostatic free energy lowering yields $\ln\gamma_\pm = -\frac{e^2 \kappa}{8\pi\epsilon_r\epsilon_0 k_B T} |z_+ z_-|$. Since Debye screening parameter $\kappa \propto \sqrt{I}$, converting to base-10 log in aqueous solution at $25^\circ\text{C}$ gives $\log_{10}\gamma_\pm = -0.509 |z_+ z_-|\sqrt{I}$.

title: Mendelian Independent Assortment Probability Rule
formulaOrRule: P(A \cap B) = P(A) \times P(B) \quad (\text{Product Rule of Independent Events})
derivationOrExplanation: Mendel's second law postulates non-homologous chromosomes segregate independently during Meiosis I anaphase. formulaOrRule: \text{Phenotypic Ratio} = 3:1 \quad (F_2 \text{ Monohybrid}), \quad \text{Genotypic Ratio} = 1:2:1
derivationOrExplanation: Gamete segregation yields $P(A) = 1/2$ and $P(a) = 1/2$. formulaOrRule: \text{Test Cross Ratio} = 1:1 \quad (\text{Monohybrid}), \quad \text{Test Cross Ratio} = 1:1:1:1 \quad (\text{Dihybrid})

formulaOrRule: N_{gametes} = 2^n, \quad N_{genotypes} = 3^n, \quad N_{phenotypes} = 2^n

title: Hardy-Weinberg Principle of Population Genetics
formulaOrRule: p + q = 1, \quad p^2 + 2pq + q^2 = 1
derivationOrExplanation: Godfrey Harold Hardy and Wilhelm Weinberg (1908) analyzed random union of gametes: pool contains fraction $p$ of $A$ alleles and $q$ of $a$ alleles ($p + q = 1$). Random mating produces genotypes by binomial expansion: $(p + q)^2 = p^2 (AA) + 2pq (Aa) + q^2 (aa) = 1$. The next generation allele frequency is $p' = p^2 + \frac{1}{2}(2pq) = p(p+q) = p$, proving frequencies remain invariant.

title: Exponential (Malthusian) Population Growth Model
formulaOrRule: \frac{dN}{dt} = r N \implies N(t) = N_0 e^{r t}, \quad t_{double} = \frac{\ln 2}{r}
derivationOrExplanation: Per capita growth rate is constant: $\frac{1}{N}\frac{dN}{dt} = r \implies \frac{dN}{dt} = rN$. Separating variables: $\frac{dN}{N} = r\,dt$. Integrating from $t=0$ ($N=N_0$) to $t$: $\ln(N/N_0) = rt \implies N(t) = N_0 e^{rt}$. Doubling time condition: $2N_0 = N_0 e^{rt_{double}} \implies t_{double} = \frac{\ln 2}{r} \approx \frac{0.693}{r}$.

title: Logistic (Verhulst-Pearl) Population Growth Model
formulaOrRule: \frac{dN}{dt} = r N \left(1 - \frac{N}{K}\right) = r N \left(\frac{K - N}{K}\right)
derivationOrExplanation: Pierre Verhulst and Raymond Pearl modified exponential model by introducing density-dependent feedback: environmental resistance increases linearly with population density, scaling factor $(1 - N/K)$. When $N \ll K$, $(1 - N/K) \approx 1$ (exponential growth). As $N \to K$, growth rate $\frac{dN}{dt} \to 0$. Integrating via partial fractions yields sigmoid S-curve: $N(t) = \frac{K}{1 + \left(\frac{K - N_0}{N_0}\right)e^{-rt}}$.

title: Master Theorem for Divide-and-Conquer Recurrences
formulaOrRule: T(n) = a T(n/b) + f(n) \implies T(n) = \Theta(n^{\log_b a}) \quad (\text{if } f(n) = O(n^{\log_b a - \epsilon}))

Case 1: If leaf work dominates ($f(n) = O(n^{\log_b a - \epsilon})$), $T(n) = \Theta(n^{\log_b a})$. Case 2: If work is uniformly distributed at each level ($f(n) = \Theta(n^{\log_b a} \log^k n)$), $T(n) = \Theta(n^{\log_b a} \log^{k+1} n)$. Case 3: If root work dominates ($f(n) = \Omega(n^{\log_b a + \epsilon})$ and regularity condition holds), $T(n) = \Theta(f(n))$.

title: Binary Cross-Entropy Loss (Log Loss)
formulaOrRule: L_{BCE} = -\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^N \left[y_i \ln \hat{y}_i + (1 - y_i)\ln(1 - \hat{y}_i)\right]
derivationOrExplanation: Assuming Bernoulli distribution for class probability: $P(y|x) = \hat{y}^y (1 - \hat{y})^{1-y}$. Likelihood over $N$ independent samples is $L = \prod_{i=1}^N \hat{y}_i^{y_i}(1 - \hat{y}_i)^{1 - y_i}$. Taking natural logarithm: $\ln L = \sum [y_i \ln\hat{y}_i + (1 - y_i)\ln(1 - \hat{y}_i)]$. Minimizing negative log-likelihood per sample yields Binary Cross-Entropy loss $L_{BCE} = -\frac{1}{N}\sum [y_i\ln\hat{y}_i + (1 - y_i)\ln(1 - \hat{y}_i)]$.
